config.name: photonic_focus_heatmaps
config.description: Grayscale print tuning for the focusing experiments: each item is one experiment with its Initial and Final camera heatmaps, printed in several grayscale variations per round, scanned by the user and judged by the agents to pick a better gamma. Only gamma is tuned, in all three rounds.

page.description: Each page shows items_per_page items, each printed in variations_per_item variations, so one page has items_per_page x variations_per_item tiles.

panels.description: The figures inside one item. For this project an item has 2 heatmap panels: the Initial and the Final camera image.

limits.description: The value limits that map data to gray are computed once from all panels of an item together and stay fixed for the whole calibration session, so the panels of an item stay comparable and only gamma changes between rounds.

gamma.description: Tone curve applied to the normalized data; values below 1 brighten the low values, above 1 darken them. Test values are spaced on a log scale.

gray_levels.description: The printed gray for the lowest (dark) and highest (light) data values, where 0 means black and 1 means white. Not tuned: always printed with the defaults, dark 0.0 and light 1.0.

steps.description: Number of discrete gray bands. 0 means smooth (no banding). Not tuned: always printed with the default 0 (smooth).

invert.description: If true, high data values print dark instead of light. Not tuned; set by hand if needed.

variation_rules.description: Each item's variations include reference_count copies of the best settings so far; the other variations change only the parameter of the current round. A shared parameter gets the same test values in every item.

references.description: Printed on every page for reading the scan: gray_patches patches evenly spaced from 0 to 1, paper_refs blank paper areas, one full black patch, and markers corner markers for aligning the scan, with a page code that identifies the page and round.

scan.description: Requirements for the scanned page the user returns.
